newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower for third day.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower for third day.

text.p: Swiss shares ended lower on Monday for the third session in a row, continuing what dealers described as a welcome consolidation after a stretch of strong gains.
Opening losses on Wall Street, insecurity ahead of a host of U.S. economic data later in the week and a slightly easier U.S. dollar were seen as main reasons for the decline.
"But overall, there is no negative sentiment in the market," one trader added.
Financials were bolstered by firming futures on government bonds. Further developments were seen depending on Wall Street.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) lost 27.5 points, or 0.61 percent, to 4,460.1.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) fell 13.57 points, or 0.48 percent, to 2,837.99.
Investors also kept back ahead of U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before the House of Representatives on Wednesday, one trader noted.

One trader said industrials may also be pressured because investor's earlier high expectations about the positive effect of an easing Swiss franc for Swiss exporters gave way to a more sober assessment after last week's results of SMH and ABB.
ABB and SMH recovered from recent losses. ABB added five francs to 1,681. SMH bearer shares jumped 14 francs to 854.

Banks generally performed better than the market, but most-active UBS fell four francs to 1,322. Stocks of CS Group, whose 1996 results are due on Wednesday, added 0.50 francs to 157.75 francs. SBC also firmed.
Novartis registered shares gave up 14 francs to 1,672. Roche slumped 225 francs to 12,190. Share rights on Ciba Specialty Chemicals fell 1.35 francs to 92.
